title: A Pilot Feasibility Study of Pulsed Electric Field (PEF) Tumor Priming Before Lisocabtagene Maraleucel (Liso-cel) in Relapsed/Refractory B-cell Malignancies
official: A Pilot Feasibility Study of Pulsed Electric Field (PEF) Tumor Priming Before Lisocabtagene Maraleucel (Liso-cel) in Relapsed/Refractory B-cell Malignancies
summary: This is an experimental single-arm, open-label, interventional pilot feasibility study designed to evaluate the safety, feasibility, and biologic impact of pulsed electric field (PEF) ablation administered during the CAR T-cell vein-to-vein interval. We will enroll 5 subjects in this pilot trial. The primary objective is to understand the feasibility of the intervention in the proposed study population. We will measure this by Calculation of the percentage of subjects who receive PEF ablation and successfully receive a CAR T-cell infusion. The secondary objectives include metabolic tumor volume dynamics, CAR-T expansion and persistence via CareDx, cytokine/immune profiling across key timepoints, and spatial (abscopal) response of treated vs untreated lesions. These will be measured in the days following PEF ablation with IRE and CAR-T infusion, up to 6 months following CAR-T infusion.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Biopsy-proven relapsed or progressive DLBCL, MCL, MZL, FL, or CLL/SLL meeting an FDA-approved indication for liso-cel infusion.
2. Presence of disease on imaging including at least one disease site in a peripheral node safe for PEF ablation as determined by treating interventional radiologist.
3. Willingness to participate in clinical trial and provide informed consent
4. Adequate organ function as assessed by standard institution protocols and US prescribing information label for comorbidities, heart, and lung function to undergo FDA-approved CAR Tcell therapy as determined by institution
5. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0-2
6. Age 19 years or older

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Subject is unsafe for PEF ablation or no safe site is available as determined by investigator and/or interventional radiologist
2. The patient has an implanted electronic device or severe cardiac dysfunction.
3. Diagnosis is primary CNS lymphoma (secondary CNS lymphoma with additional systemic site is allowed)
4. Requirement for concurrent high-dose methotrexate
5. Secondary active malignancy that has not been in remission for at least 2 years. This excludes non-melanoma skin cancer, definitively treated stage 1 solid tumor with low risk of recurrence, and curatively treated localized prostate cancer.
6. Pregnant or nursing women
7. Uncontrolled medical, psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical conditions that do not permit compliance with the protocol, as determined by investigator
8. Unwillingness to follow procedures required in the protocol
9. Inadequate organ or hematologic conditions that prohibit the use of lymphodepleting chemotherapy
10. Use of Confirmation that lymphoma-directed therapy is not planned to be administered within 14 days of T-cell pheresis.
11. Previous significant adverse reaction to general anesthesia precluding patient from PEF ablation at the discretion of the interventional radiologist or investigator.
